As TD 07W continues to move W away from the Marianas, the southeast 
inflow will keep scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
possible for Guam throughout tonight before improving to isolated 
coverage on Saturday. As for the CNMI, decided to keep low-end (30%)
scattered showers but omitted thunderstorm potential due to 
satellite trends showing any possible convection being sheared off. 
Model guidance shows the northeastern extent of TD 07W's tail 
reinvigorating tomorrow, so the CNMI will remain at scattered shower 
coverage throughout Saturday afternoon. High pressure will follow TD 
07W, so drier conditions are expected for the Marianas starting 
Saturday night. Winds may become light and variable starting Sunday, 
so island-effect showers and isolated thunderstorms may be possible 
in the afternoon hours for all islands through at least the first 
half of next week.

Marine...
No altimetry passes are available near the islands, so combined seas
are inferred to be up to 6 ft for Guam and up to 5 ft for the CNMI 
based on buoy data. Guam waters are mainly seeing the southeast swell
whereas the CNMI will be mainly affected by the easterly trade swell.
There is a moderate risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs at
least through the weekend. There is a moderate risk of lightning for
Guam reefs through tonight.

Tropical Systems...
As of the 1 PM ChST, the center of TD 07W was located near 13.1N,
142.5E. This is 115 miles west of Guam, and 255 miles west-southwest
of Saipan. TD 07W continues to gradually organize, with both radar
and visible imagery showing increasing convective banding associated
with the LLCC (Low-Level Circulation Center). TD 07W is forecast to
strengthen to a tropical storm tonight, possibly becoming a typhoon 
on Sunday. This cyclone will continue its west-northwest movement 
during the next 24 to 48 hours, turning more northwest with time. 
Luckily, it's traversing open waters with no inhabited land masses 
expected.

Then, we have Invest 93W (currently rated as "Sub-Low" from JTWC (the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center) that is located near 5N168E. This 
feature is bringing periods of heavy rainfall to a vast majority of 
the RMI and Kosrae, and it'll continue to do so for at least the next
48 hours (probably longer), as it drifts slowly west-northwest. 
Pohnpei is just west of this heavier rainfall, but it'll move into 
the region over the next few days. A Special Weather Statement (SPS) 
was reissued to cover this for Pohnpei and Kosrae. At Majuro, some 
locally/brief heavy rainfall is possible through tomorrow, but this 
area of heavier showers is slowly moving away. Thus, Majuro was not 
included in the SPS re-issuance.

Looking ahead in the medium range portion of the forecast (~72 to 
120 forecast hours), 93W is expected to lift more towards the
northwest. Similar to many systems earlier this year, the models may
be too fast and/or too strong in the model projections. With that
said, the Madden-Julian Oscillation will be coming into a "more
favorable position" during the last week of the month. We'll continue
to monitor forecast trends, but at this point...IT'S WAY, WAY TOO
EARLY to even take a guess how strong it'll be and which track it'll
take. 

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Folks should continue to monitor the forecast for updates at
www.weather.gov/gum, or on our office social media pages.

Eastern Micronesia...
A wet and unsettled pattern continues, as it's currently affecting 
Kosrae and a majority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Majuro
will gradually see the steadier/heavier showers shift over the next 
24 to 48 hours. Until then, Majuro will be on the "eastern fringe" 
of the scattered to numerous shower coverage.

As Invest 93W slowly moves west-northwest, locally heavier showers
will become more prominent at Pohnpei, while continuing at Kosrae.
With this in mind, locally heavy showers will likely occur from time
to time, and the previous shift's Special Weather Statement (SPS) is
in good shape. As such, similar wording was retained for Pohnpei and
Kosrae. At Majuro, being on the fringe means the likelihood of 
heavier rainfall is in the diminishing process, so the recently re-
issued SPS didn't include you given the forecast expectations 
mentioned above.

For the mariners, light to gentle winds and seas of 3 to 5 feet will
prevail the next several days. As always, isolated wind gusts near 25
knots will remain possible near any heavier shower or thunderstorm,
with visibilities reduced as well.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau and Yap, TD 07W is the main weather maker for the portion
of Western Micronesia. Yap will see conditions a bit earlier than 
Palau, but both are expected to be in the westerly intake of TD 07W 
moves west. This will bring scattered to numerous showers and
